description: Helps you decide which accounts to work first. You give your accounts with fit, intent and relationship scores from 0 to 100 and a timing, plus optional weights. You get a ranked list from a weighted score, with a tier for each account, the points its timing earned and the factor that added the most points. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Without accounts, it returns the scoring framework and an example input. Missing account scores default to 50. Invalid ranges or all-zero weights return an error. Use this instead of icp_scoring_model when you have accounts and numeric scores ready to rank.

accounts.description: List of accounts to prioritize. Each account: name, fit score (0 to 100), intent signals (0 to 100), relationship (0 to 100), timing (now, soon, later or unknown). Format is a JSON array. For example, [{"name":"an approved anonymous manufacturer","fit_score":30,"intent_signals":30}].

items.description: Format is a JSON object. For example, {"name":"an approved anonymous manufacturer","fit_score":30,"intent_signals":30}.

fit_score.description: 0 to 100. Left out, 50 is used. Format is a JSON number. For example, 30.

intent_signals.description: 0 to 100 (0 scores zero). Left out, 50 is used. Format is a JSON number. For example, 30.

name.description: Format is text. For example, "an approved anonymous manufacturer".

relationship.description: 0 to 100, based on existing connections. Left out, 50 is used. Format is a JSON number. For example, 30.

timing.description: Buying horizon: now, soon, later or unknown (100, 70, 40 and 50 points respectively). Equivalent phrases are read by clause; denied or conflicting horizons remain unknown. Confirm the horizon with the user. Format is text. For example, "soon".

company.description: Optional: your company or product name, so the answer can name it. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

prioritization_weights.description: Optional custom weights in percent for fit, intent, relationship and timing. A missing weight uses its default (40, 30, 15, 15); the tool does not check that the weights sum to 100. Format is a JSON object. For example, {"fit":30,"intent":30,"relationship":30}.

fit.description: Format is a JSON number. For example, 30.

intent.description: Format is a JSON number. For example, 30.

relationship.description: Format is a JSON number. For example, 30.

timing.description: Format is a JSON number. For example, 30.

product_category.description: Optional: what you sell (for example "spend management software"), used for sector notes. The arithmetic does not use it. Format is text.

name: account_prioritization
title: Account Prioritization
